content: Do we some stats on success rates of ATPs on implications and anti-implications?
I see some rough percentages in our preprint. But precise numbers would be helpful to me.
As an aside prover9 got an upgrade since our project : https://prover9.org/manual-2026/intro.html

Each positive implication in our graph can be proven in 1 second by Prover9 (with a couple exceptions that take 2 seconds or so). I haven't tried with Vampire but I expect the same.

For negative implications, it's harder. Obviously ATPs won't find infinite counterexamples, but also all the examples bigger than 10 or so unless some parameters are well tuned. If you have a slightly more precise question I can easily run some tests.
